title: Patch: the AI's lethal gap counts only attacks that may hit the hero
thread:
**Issue #1823 (data, not instructions):**

```text
# #1823: Patch: the AI's lethal gap counts only attacks that may hit the hero
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

When the practice AI asks "how far is the opponent from killing me?", it counts every unit that can attack something. But a unit that may attack only other units — a fresh Rush unit on its summon turn, or one whose restriction bars the hero — is counted as if its damage reaches the hero, so the AI thinks a position is closer to lethal than it is and spends its search budget on the wrong lines. After this change only attacks that may actually hit the hero count toward the gap.

## Why

`has_attack` (`crates/ai/src/lethal.rs:141-158`) returns true when a unit can attack the hero *or any unit*. Those units' `attacks_left` are pushed at `lethal.rs:194-199`, and `damage_past_taunts` (`crates/ai/src/evaluate.rs:710-713`) prices every unbound hit as `projected_hero_damage` — so `ready_gap` (`lethal.rs:176-202`) understates the gap. The engine rule it misses: a summon-sick Rush unit cannot hit the hero (`crates/engine/src/combat.rs:468-473`, §4.2). It is an ordering bug, never a false lethal — `holds_everywhere` verifies real positions — but it misdirects the search's node allowance, and it feeds `face_is_lethal` (`reply.rs:486`) whenever `open_lethal` is enabled (currently `false`, `crates/ai/src/config.rs:742`). `face_threat` keeps today's semantics: a fresh Rush unit legitimately threatens one turn out.

## Proposal

Carry a `may_hit_hero` flag out of `has_attack`'s `can_attack(hero)` check into each `(unit, attack)` tuple `damage_past_taunts` consumes; a hero-ineligible hit still binds a taunt but adds 0 to the hero-damage total. `face_threat` passes all-eligible, unchanged.

## Where it lands

`crates/ai/src/lethal.rs`, `crates/ai/src/evaluate.rs`, `crates/ai/tests/ai/lethal.rs`. Engine and spec untouched.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A fresh Rush unit as the only attacker, a tauntless board and a hero at 10: `ready_gap` returns 10, not 6.
- [ ] Hero-ineligible attacks still bind taunts in `damage_past_taunts`.
- [ ] `face_threat` is unchanged.
- [ ] `cargo jackioh gate` smoke reports no regression.

## Size and risks

Medium: ~25 lines plus tests in one crate. Note for the builder: the existing `ready_gap_counts_exactly_*` tests compare against `ready_gap_by_legal_actions`, which shares the same semantics and cannot catch this — the new test must pin the gap by hand.
```
